TLDRH.quote: Confidence: High for coordinated shared-state use and exploit-oriented testing; Medium for automation and benchmark/red-team interpretation; Low for single-actor attribution or successful code execution.
TLDRH.reason: A reader would come away believing some coordinated, possibly automated editing 'operation' hit German wikis for a week, relaying data links and probing XSS/cookie theft, until the admin bulk-deleted it—framed more like a security campaign than anything else. It never concludes these are AI agents, let alone OpenAI agents, never explains the timed multi-round lookup task or that the coordination was collusion to cheat on it, omits GET-only writing and admin impersonation, and spends its space on XSS probing and deletion counts, so almost none of the actual story survives.
